questions.q: With what does David say he will sing praises?
questions.a: David says he will sing and make music with his whole being.

questions.q: How does David describe how great is Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness?
questions.a: David says that Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness is so great that it is like the distance between the heavens and the earth.

questions.q: Where does David ask for God’s glory to be exalted?
questions.a: David asks that God’s glory be exalted all over the earth.

questions.q: What has God spoken about Ephraim and Judah?
questions.a: God spoke of the tribe of Ephraim as his protection in battle and Judah is where his kings come from.

questions.q: What does God say he will do over Philistia?
questions.a: God says he will shout triumphantly because he has defeated the people of Philistia.

questions.q: Whose help does David say is futile?
questions.a: David asks for God’s help because man’s help is futile.

questions.q: How does David describe his triumph with God’s help?
questions.a: David says that with God’s help they will win, and God will enable them to defeat their enemies.

commentary.text: —We may usefully select passages from different psalms, as here, Ps 57; 60, to help our devotions, and enliven our gratitude. When the heart is firm in faith and love, the tongue, being employed in grateful praises, is our glory. Every gift of the Lord honours and profits the possessor, as it is employed in God's service and to his glory. Believers may pray with assured faith and hope, for all the blessings of salvation; which are secured to them by the faithful promise and covenant of God. Then let them expect from him help in every trouble, and victory in every conflict. Whatever we do, whatever we gain, God must have all the glory. Lord, visit all our souls with this salvation, with this favour which thou bearest to thy chosen people.
